body: Treat the blood pressure advice with extreme caution as they use 120/70 as a base line. This is fine for a 45 year old but not for people away from this age range. There is no adjustment for ageing. This can lead to older persons with perfectly normal blood pressure seeking medication that can cause more harms than good. As a person ages blood vessels naturally become less flexible and blood pressure rises. Treat any information from this app as guidance and if there are sudden changes then seek qualified medical advice. Do not treat any information as actionable as it could lead to harms.

title: More notable for missing features than successes
body:
There are so many things this app *could* do… but it successfully does very few of them. Noticeable omissions are:

- simple one- or two-tap logging processes for cycle tracking, medication, symptoms and other items

- customisable or editable symptoms lists (if you don’t have a symptom the devs are familiar with you can’t log the symptom at all) for tracking chronic or recurrent problems

- simple and easy food diary linked to a suitable bar code database

- correlation tracking between symptoms and medications/supplements/diet to measure benefits and side effects

- family health tracking (I can’t track my kids’ health in this app and have to use other ones)

- formally diagnosed conditions (e.g. I might want to track how a chronic condition is affected by getting a minor illness or how often I get particular types of illness or injury)

Without these features, the effort of adding data to Apple Health just doesn’t really pay off and third party apps are a better bet. I only gave two stars because some of the Watch integration and sleep tracking features have improved in recent iterations. But c’mon. Considering how late to the party Apple were on cycle tracking, and how many years they’ve had since figuring out that half their customers might find it useful, the current state of it is a poor effort.

I currently use a Shortcut to manually write the intake data, but it would be great if this happened automatically when I tap “Taken”, or if Medications events could act as triggers for Shortcuts.

There’s no way 🙅🏽‍♀️ to switch to a natural cycle without deleting any data (which I’m not even going to do 🙅🏽‍♀️☝🏽) 

This isn’t a minor issue - it’s a huge blind spot and design flaw that shows how little the designers understand real women’s anatomy and health. 

Millions of women like me come off the pill every single year which is very normal. We shouldn’t even have to erase our cycle history just to get accurate cycle predictions. 

Apple: Add a simple “I’m off the pill” toggle/option. We definitely deserve much better results than locking this explanation behind a paywall is quite frankly unacceptable and misleading. Women should not have to pay for advanced essential functionality. 

I urge you to fix this immediately and rethink how your app is designed.

title: Poor for weight management and general Fitness Reporting
body:
The Apple Watch is excellent and the Fitness App is also good.  However the reporting/analytics using the Health App needs a lot of work.  It records the ‘numbers’ but there is no analysis.  The apps that track key metrics such as calorie intake (I.e. MyFitnessPal and and training readiness such as Athlytic are separate.

There is no native way to get the same info from the Health App.  Even basic fitness info such as calorie deficit or surplus have to be calculated manually.  The app also provides no insight or recommended adjustment to your fitness programme.

It’s a bit like having a spreadsheet with no formulas and no easy way to read reports.   So there are good foundations but little polish.

Other companies such as Fitbit (and I think Whoop) have managed to consolidate and report on this info.  I prefer Apple hardware and would like to stay within the Apple eco system especially with a Fitness or Health app that provided a single view.

I have found Athlytic to be the closet to Fitbit (and I believe Whoop) and it can reference the calorie info from MyFitness Pal and your workout data from Apple Health/Fitness apps.  This means it can easily show calorie surplus /deficit.  It also provides easy to read sleep analysis (using data from Apple health/Apple Watch).  The Athlytic subscription cost isn’t too expensive but I think either the Apple health app or fitness could provide the same features with some development - there is also the fact that I am already paying for the Fitness+ subscription.

Maybe Apple could buy/work with Athlytic and integrate  the features into the Apple Fitness app and keep the Health app as a ‘background data collector’ app?

The Analytics and reporting elements should also be available on iPads and Macs as they have larger screens and are easier to read .

Many thanks.

title: Please please make this better!!
body:
Using this app mainly for cycle tracking, but also for tracking fitness. Really disappointed at how clunky it is, and the very poor and unorganised layout. The algorithm is also very inaccurate - I.e. predicted period does not change when logging clear signs of ovulation. At the minute I am using a third party app to feed in the information as it is much more user friendly, but I am concerned about my data which is why I would prefer via apple.
I also think the sleep tracker is really inaccurate. Lots of sleep logged when I have actually been awake, while wearing the new Apple Watch as well. 

 Suggestions:
- big big improvement in AI and algorithms to track and predict ovulation/period
- ability to view cycle as calendar 
- view of what day in your cycle you are on at a glance
- nearly having cycle tracking as a stand along app would be better as it is such a big thing for half the population! 
- wrist temp should be used alongside cycle data to help correlate between period/cervical mucous changes to allow for better tracking
- wrist temp displayed as the temperature rather than change from baseline - my baseline started just before I ovulated and therefore baseline is not accurate. Not sure if this will be my baseline forever or if AI will sort this issue out.
- organising favourites in summary by group rather than by alphabetical order

I’m desperate for health to be great, but at the minute it is a big flop 👎🏻

title: Surprisingly Awful!
body:
To say I’m shocked at how bad this app is, would be an understatement. It’s overly complex, unattractive and poorly thought out. The sleep tracking is terrible. Unless you set a sleep schedule it doesn’t track your sleep.  Not everyone wants a sleep schedule!  And when it is tracking, it’s often incorrect and mixes up time in bed with being asleep, or vice versa. It doesn’t track type of sleep, e.g. REM v deep sleep, and doesn’t tell you how many hours/minutes of sleep you get, you have to work that out for yourself. 
The exercise and non exercise calorie trackers are separate rather than in one place, WHY?? The heart health tells you a whole load of info but doesn’t inform you what it means, e.g. it gives a score for how fast your heart rate drops after you stop exercising but not what the National average or mean/norm is. Much of the heart health tracking is similar, lots of scores and info but not what any of it means, so nothing to compare with. Guess I need to go and get a medical degree in heart health! 
I really, really dislike it and in comparison to Fitbit health tracker and app, Apple Health is useless and a very poorly designed offer. I will not replace my Apple Watch once it wears out because of the app. I’ll go back to Fitbit!

title: Apple Health App - Feedback
body:
To the Apple Developers of the Health App. 

In certain ways I find it extremely helpful if I can write a small note when inputting manual data. An example would be in the Blood Pressure data. 

The input ‘Add Data’ in this case limits the user to fixed strings (a date, a time a reading).

The addition of a simple Note text box would be of immense value. Limited, say to 20 Characters.

A high reading cannot be expanded on. It may be higher than normal but there’s a good reason, a note text box would allow me to ‘qualify’ such an anomaly.
 
This feedback is applicable to all aspects of the Health App where it isn’t obvious why numbers are unusual or unexpected. I would then rate as ***** Stars.

The App is an extremely well developed piece of work, and I’m enormously grateful to be able to record my health activity, using it with my Apple Watch. Maybe you could consider this suggestion in a future update, thanks guys.
